title: AutoMIL: Automated Multiple Instance Learning for Whole-Slide Image Classification
authors: Jonas Waibel, Frank Kramer, Dominik M\"uller
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32452v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Developing multiple instance learning pipelines for the classification of whole-slide images involves many interdependent design decisions and expertise in both pathology and machine learning. We present AutoMIL, an open-source framework that applies principles from the field of automated machine learning to tackle this task by automating integral pipeline steps, such as preprocessing, training and evaluation. abstract:

abstract:

Abstract: This paper presents a new method for the zero-shot open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) of 3D automotive lidar data. Given a 3D network distilled from a 2D Vision Foundation Model (VFM), we then label a point cloud by matching 3D point features with 2D image features of these prototypes. Abstract: DETR-style detectors use one-to-one bipartite matching during training to assign object queries to ground-truth objects, enabling end-to-end set prediction without non-maximum suppression (NMS). authors: Oron Nir, Eliyahu Strugo, Ariel Shamir
abstract:
arXiv:2610.28941v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Clothes-Changing Person Re-Identification (CC-ReID) remains challenging due to drastic appearance shifts across outfits. Most prior works devise biometric signal-extraction heuristics to enhance inter-person variance, e.g., using segmentation masks, while leaving intra-person variance uncontrolled. Extensive experiments show that MINER improves retrieval across CC-ReID benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance on four datasets and ranking among the leaders in all three tracks of the open TVRID RGB-Depth ReID challenge.

Abstract: Pathology workflows require multiple visual judgments about the same slide, from identifying tumor type to assessing grade and invasion. Abstract: Reliable visual perception is essential for safe autonomous underwater exploration. abstract:
arXiv:2610.40905v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Histopathology foundation models learn rich embedding representations, but their internal structure remains difficult to inspect. Concept-level interpretability is particularly relevant in computational pathology because pathologists reason through recurring morphological and tissue-level patterns, including tissue architecture, cellular morphology, staining variation, and artifacts. In this work, we investigate whether sparse autoencoders (SAEs) can decompose embeddings from histopathology foundation models into sparse latent features suitable for expert-assisted interpretation. authors: Nishi Kanta Paul, Md Shihabul Islam Shovo, Md Mostafijur Rahman, Jamil Fayyad
abstract:

Abstract: Vision-language agents equipped with tools expose intermediate outputs for inspection and comparison with the model's reasoning, which may offer safety benefits over single-shot models. This paper tests that potential benefit when the sensor reading itself is untrusted, so that the tool and reasoning channels share a common visual fault. We consider a dermatology agent based on segmentation, contrastive retrieval, and an iterative vision-language reasoner and define a coupling taxonomy that distinguishes single-channel errors from joint errors that agree or disagree. On PAD-UFES-20, we show that typographic injection produces detectable directional retrieval capture, whereas physical corruption does not. title: Let LiDAR Decide Where to Look: Geometry-Measured Token Selection for Efficient Sparse Latent World Models
authors: Zeping Zhang, Zhuoya Zhao, Robert Lagani\`ere
abstract:
arXiv:2610.40935v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-centric autonomous driving models encode thousands of image tokens per frame, yet most depict sky, buildings, or empty road---content irrelevant to planning. Worse, these tokens dilute the planner's attention: we show that randomly discarding 75% of tokens already outperforms the dense model, because the planner can concentrate on the remaining driving-critical content. Building on this finding, we present Geometry-Aware Token Selection (GATS), which uses LiDAR and radar point projections to select a small fraction of image tokens before the vision backbone runs. Because the selector operates on measured 3D geometry rather than visual features, the backbone encodes only the selected patches, cutting end-to-end FLOPs by up to $18\times$. title: AVID: A Weakly Aligned RGB-Infrared Dataset and Perturbation Benchmark for Tiny Aerial Targets
authors: Dharini Raghavan, Vishnu Rao, Sethu Selvi S
abstract:
arXiv:2610.40949v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-range detection of small drones is complicated by their visual similarity to birds and by the limited detail available from ground-based cameras. Combining visible and infrared observations offers complementary information, but their usefulness depends on target size, cross-modal alignment, and image quality. We present AVID, a benchmark for studying these factors using real RGB-infrared bird-drone surveillance footage originating from the Drone Detection Dataset and curated for the IEEE ICIP 2025 Video and Image Processing Cup. AVID comprises 32,040 corresponding frame pairs from 115 videos, with 35,952 existing bird and drone annotations at $320\times256$ resolution. title: Segment Anything Pancreas: A Unified MRI Segmentation Model for Pancreatic Cancer Radiotherapy
authors: Zach Eidex, Mojtaba Safari, Kundan Thind, Parag J. Parikh, Zhen Tian, Xiaofeng Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41063v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Background: Limited tumor annotations and incomplete labels across MRI datasets hinder unified segmentation of pancreatic tumors and organs at risk (OARs) for MRI-guided radiotherapy. Purpose: We propose Pancreas-MedNeXt, a unified model that segments the whole pancreas, its subregions, tumors, and surrounding OARs from one MRI volume. Methods: The model uses a shared MedNeXt encoder-decoder with supervised whole-pancreas and subregion pretraining, followed by multitask fine-tuning. Three output heads predict the pancreatic subregions, tumor, and OARs (stomach, duodenum, kidneys). An annotation-aware loss allows training on partially labeled data without treating unannotated structures as background. title: Single-Annotation, Multi-Hypothesis Segmentation with Semantic-Spatial Residual Banks
authors: Armin Dadras, Robert Sablatnig, Franziska Proksa, Markus Seidl
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41069v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-rater segmentation datasets show that a single image can admit several valid masks, yet most training sets expose only one annotation per image. We study single-annotation multi-hypothesis segmentation: each training image exposes one fixed mask, while the model must return a finite bank that covers held-out human annotations at test time. Our experiments reveal a representation tradeoff. Banks learned directly from images recover variations in local boundaries and extent but lose structural hypotheses, whereas frozen semantic features preserve structural grouping but underrepresent spatial variation. We introduce the Semantic-Spatial Residual Bank (SSRB), which freezes a semantic bank trained with balanced assignments and learns a residual from the image for each hypothesis. title: CompoSET: A Controlled Single-Edit Benchmark for Vision-Language Compositionality
authors: Laure Delisle, Pietro Perona
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41118v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language compositionality is the ability to identify which properties, relations, quantities, and states bind to which entities in both an image and a caption, and to match those bindings across modalities. Existing benchmarks evaluate this ability through image-text matching: a model ranks candidate image-caption match similarities and succeeds when the correct match comes on top. In such datasets, paired images differ by more than a single binding: scene, layout, and content all differ, with 97% of pixels changing on average. Such pairs do not isolate compositionality: results are confounded by global image differences. We introduce Compositional Single-EdiT (CompoSET), a benchmark dataset in which each base image-caption pair has an edited counterpart, or foil, that preserves the scene but differs by a single controlled edit, such as color, count, spatial relation, or object state. title: Beyond CLIP: Calibrated (Few-Shot) Defect Detection With System One Decision Models
authors: Fadel M. Megahed, Ying-Ju Chen
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41199v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cameras and vision sensors are widely used for product and process inspection in manufacturing environments. Traditionally, this process required thousands of images of both nominal and defective products to train such models. Recent research shows that vision transformer (ViT) models, such as CLIP, can reduce this requirement to 50-100 images per nominal and defective class. However, collecting even 50 defective images can be difficult in high-yield or low-volume manufacturing processes. In this paper, we examine the utility of two recently proposed structured decision models (Jev and Clef-Flash) in applications using as few as k=2 reference images per class at inference. title: Shifting Focus by Reliability: Geometric Fusion Modulation for Robust RGB-T Detection
authors: Liuyin Shi, Chengqi Li, Wenbo He
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41204v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: RGB-thermal (RGB-T) object detectors combine visible and thermal imagery for robust detection, but signal corruption in either stream can substantially degrade accuracy. Restoration-based methods incur significant latency and do not consistently improve downstream accuracy, raising a more direct question: rather than restoring corrupted inputs, can we efficiently adapt the detector to their varying signal quality? Conventional PEFT offers an efficient route, but its input-independent corrections cannot track diverse test-time corruptions. Our controlled corruption sweeps show that corruption types have similar effects near clean conditions but diverge increasingly with severity, motivating corruption-aware, per-input adaptation. title: ReVEAL: Eliciting Role-Aware Latent Visual Evidence from MLLMs for Reasoning Video Object Segmentation
authors: Zhongyuan Bao, Cunjie He, Lejun Zhang, Zenglin Xu, Yanwei Fu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41257v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reasoning video object segmentation (ReVOS) requires segmenting the target specified by an implicit query throughout a video. Existing MLLM-based methods typically require costly cross-model alignment, tying MLLM training to a downstream segmentation model. We present ReVEAL, a decoupled thinking-with-video framework for ReVOS that elicits role-aware latent visual evidence from MLLM reasoning to directly guide segmentation. ReVEAL introduces Visual Evidence Tokens (VETs) into video reasoning to associate necessary visual regions or entities with target, background, or distractor roles, while a Dynamic Attention Layer Router adaptively aggregates VET-to-video attention across layers into role-specific grounding evidence. title: Task-Performance Routing for Multi-Teacher Distillation in CT Medical Image Segmentation
authors: Jiaye Yang, Yao Liu, Die Dai, Hanwen Zhang, Peiyuan Jiang, Qiao Liu, Yutong Xie, Peng Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41362v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Pre-trained models offer complementary strengths in CT organ segmentation, but their relative accuracy varies across organs and spatial regions. Multi-teacher knowledge distillation can combine these strengths in a single student, yet global or instance-level teacher weights overlook variation within a 3D volume. We propose Task-Performance Routing (TPR), which uses region-wise segmentation errors to determine teacher weights during training without learned routing parameters. In hard regions, TPR favors teachers with lower prediction errors; in easy regions, it uses uniform weights to combine their knowledge. A hierarchical spatial partition provides fine-grained routing in shallow encoder stages and coarse-grained routing in deep stages. title: Beyond Trial-and-Error: A Geospatial-Guided Active Reasoning Framework for Robust Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation
authors: Jiawei Ge, Wenkang Gong, Jiuxin Cao, Bo Liu, Lei Cui, Haoran Wang, Xuelin Zhu, Biwei Cao, Chang Liu, Chen Feng, Ioannis Patras
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41446v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires UAVs to locate language-specified goals in large-scale urban environments, where objects often appear small and visually ambiguous from high-altitude viewpoints. Existing methods largely follow a reactive paradigm common in indoor VLN, repeatedly updating navigation states from local observations while underutilizing the geospatial structure that remains stable during navigation. As a result, visually similar distractors can cause a reactive goal search to repeatedly reinforce locally plausible goal hypotheses based on passively accumulated evidence, leading to unreliable localization. To address this, we propose GeoReasoner, a robust framework that shifts the paradigm of Aerial VLN from reactive trial-and-error to geospatial-guided active reasoning. title: BDNet: Fast-slow thinking is all you need
authors: Chenzhi Zheng, Zhuoran Zheng
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41485v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present BDNet, a hierarchical image-classification backbone built around fast image features and slow statistical references. Its baseline deformation operator (BDO) transforms the deviation of a feature from a stage-specific reference through a low-rank projection and a learned channel scale. Rather than computing pairwise token similarity, the branch operates directly on baseline-relative residuals with complexity linear in the token count. Each of four reference buffers accumulates detached stage statistics during training and remains frozen at inference. A four-stage pyramid with depths $(2,2,6,2)$ and widths $(96,192,384,768)$ yields a 20.70M-parameter classifier at $224\times224$ resolution. authors: Eliseo Fuentes-Martinez, Antonio Hidalgo-Centeno, Jorge Calvo-Zaragoza, Antonio Javier Gallego
abstract:

Abstract: Score-based multimodal music retrieval requires representations that are both discriminative within each modality and compatible across audio recordings, sheet music images, and symbolic scores. This paper investigates the effectiveness of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) for adapting pretrained music encoders and examines whether modality-specific improvements translate into better multimodal representations. We compare full fine-tuning, LoRA, and QLoRA across nine pretrained audio, image, and symbolic score encoders on TriScore and the Musical Theme Dataset. Encoders are first evaluated and selected through supervised unimodal classification, using frozen-encoder linear probing as a reference. title: Attention Maps Know When to Think: Training-Free Difficulty-Aware Chain-of-Thought for Reasoning Segmentation
authors: Chanseul Cho, Jaesung Jun, Dongheon Lee, Youngmin Ro
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41618v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting has become a standard reasoning strategy in Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), showing strong performance in complex vision-language tasks such as reasoning segmentation. However, our analysis reveals that indiscriminate CoT usage can lead to degraded performance by inducing unnecessary reasoning, a phenomenon we term overthinking. In reasoning segmentation, overthinking often leads to misalignment between the query's intent and visual grounding. To address this, we propose Difficulty-Aware Chain-of-Thought (DA-CoT), a training-free adaptive framework that selectively triggers CoT based on the input's intrinsic difficulty. authors: Alaa Alshubbak, Daniel G\"orges
abstract:

Abstract: Pose estimation is a computer vision task used to estimate a skeleton of dynamic systems to predict future movements. Most of the research in this direction is based on a supervised learning approach which requires a massive amount of labeled datasets. In this paper, a self-supervised three-stage model based on a contrastive learning approach is introduced for estimating a skeleton of dynamic construction machines; such as excavators without using any labeled images for the first stage. authors: Samuel Thomas, Daniel Tweneboah Anyimadu, Ahmed Karam Eldaly, Somaia Elsheikh, Mohammed M. Abdelsamea
abstract:

Abstract: Reliable histopathology segmentation requires models that rely on pathology-relevant structures rather than spurious background correlations. In this work, we argue that improving architectures alone is insufficient if models continue to rely on spurious correlations rather than pathology-relevant features. We introduce a causality-inspired evaluation framework based on controlled interventions that explicitly probes model sensitivity to foreground tissue structure and background/domain variation. Building on this, we propose the Causal Reliance Score (CRS), a metric that quantifies the relative sensitivity of model predictions to foreground perturbation versus background/domain variation under controlled interventions. authors: Tahar Chettaoui, Guray Ozgur, Eduarda Caldeira, Naser Damer, Fadi Boutros
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41789v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-head attention in Vision Transformers (ViTs) allows independent attention patterns across heads, but without explicit regularization, heads may learn redundant patterns rather than complementary roles. Correlation-based penalties encourage head disentanglement, yet apply uniform regularization across all training samples. In face recognition (FR), hard samples whose embeddings lie close to competing identities are critical for optimization and generalization. authors: Eunseob Choi, Kyeonghun Kim, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim
abstract:

Abstract: Average segmentation accuracy and model count do not reveal whether models fail on the same cases. We present CoFailMed, an audit of correlated failures in pretrained-encoder pools for medical segmentation. abstract:

Abstract: Vision Transformers represent each image patch through a canonical token produced under one observation condition. authors: Valentin Hassler, Jonathan Henrich, Yoha\"i-Eliel Berreby, Haoze Zhu, Alexander Ecker
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41987v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Human vision is foveated and active: resolution is highest at the fovea and falls off towards the periphery, and fixations are actively directed to locations of interest. Building a machine system that processes information in the same way lets us study gaze behavior in a controlled setting where the system's components and objectives are known. The emergence of gaze characteristics can therefore be examined systematically, which may in turn inform our understanding of biological vision. This requires a model that can sample like the fovea, handle various tasks from classification to dense prediction, and be trained concurrently with a fixation policy. In our study, we present such a system and study its capabilities and the fixation policies that emerge from it. title: Rethinking Asymmetry in Self-Supervised 3D Geometry Learning
authors: Gyeongjin Kang, Freeman Cheng, Botao Ye, Weijie Lyu, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Eunbyung Park
abstract:
arXiv:2610.42092v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-supervised learning relies on asymmetry between what a model observes and what it must explain. Recent methods learn 3D geometry from unposed images by predicting cameras and scene structure, then rendering held-out views. To avoid trivial solutions, they impose this asymmetry in the input space, restricting how views interact through separate branches or masked attention. When a held-out view lies between context views, the context already constrains the geometry it observes. We therefore impose the asymmetry in the 3D representation space, excluding held-out views only from the reconstructed scene while a shared backbone uses all views for correspondence. abstract:

abstract:

title: Generalizable Multiscale Segmentation of Heterogeneous Map Collections
authors: Remi Petitpierre
abstract:
arXiv:2603.05037v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Historical map collections are highly diverse in style, scale, and geographic focus, often consisting of many single-sheet documents. Yet most work in map recognition focuses on specialist models tailored to homogeneous map series. In contrast, this article aims to develop generalizable semantic segmentation models and a shared class ontology. We introduce Semap, a new open benchmark dataset comprising 1,439 manually annotated patches designed to reflect the variety of historical map documents. We also evaluate a segmentation workflow that combines procedural data synthesis with multiscale integration. Under the harmonized benchmarks considered here, this workflow attains the strongest performance among the evaluated approaches and viably learns from heterogeneous map data. title: MuCALD-SplitFed: Causal-Latent Diffusion for Privacy-Preserving Multi-Task Split-Federated Medical Image Segmentation
authors: Chamani Shiranthika, Hadi Hadizadeh, Parvaneh Saeedi
abstract:
arXiv:2605.04108v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Federated Learning enables decentralized training by aggregating model updates across clients without sharing raw data, while Split Federated Learning further partitions the model between clients and a server to reduce computation and communication at the client side. However, decentralized medical institutions rarely operate on a single shared task, making standard Federated and SplitFed collaborations poorly aligned with real clinical workflows. Multi-task FL extends these frameworks by allowing clients to handle different tasks, but often introduces instability and privacy vulnerabilities. This study proposes \textbf{MuCALD-SplitFed}, a multi-task SplitFed framework that integrates causal representation learning and latent diffusion. title: DAUPNet: Domain-Aware Uncertainty Modeling for Reliable Prototype Discrimination in Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation
authors: Lei Yuan, Zhongxu Hu, Jingyi Wen, Pengxing Yi
abstract:

Abstract: Cross-domain few-shot semantic segmentation (CD-FSS) has predominantly been formulated as learning domain-invariant representations or improving support-query correspondence. Nevertheless, large domain shifts still make prototype matching unreliable: inconsistent hierarchical responses corrupt the support representation, deterministic prototypes cannot express boundary and appearance ambiguity, and treating prototypes with different reliability equally during optimization weakens foreground-background separation. We therefore propose DAUPNet, a unified framework that reformulates cross-domain prototype matching as uncertainty-aware prototype discrimination. title: One Step Is Optimal: Unconditional Rectified Flows as Noise2Noise Denoisers for Low-Dose CT
authors: Timothy Sereda, Debesh Jha
abstract:
arXiv:2609.31670v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We study rectified flows for denoising without clean training targets. For an unconditional rectified flow trained on Noise2Noise pairs, the optimal velocity field yields the minimum mean squared error (MMSE) denoiser in one step. In a jointly Gaussian model, we show that integrating the flow before applying its denoising readout increases error with integration time. The flow transports between noisy distributions, so its endpoint is not a clean-image estimate. Experiments on low-dose CT and Gaussian-corrupted natural images follow this pattern: one-step flow performs similarly to direct regression on the same pairs, whereas additional Euler steps reduce PSNR. authors: Yunus Serhat B{\i}\c{c}ak\c{c}{\i}
abstract:

Abstract: Semantic segmentation of street panoramas can support detailed descriptions of urban environments, yet small datasets and unequal training costs make model selection difficult. This paper documents the two stages of a submission to the PalmCity challenge. In the first stage, nine pretrained segmentation systems are compared using approximately equal computation budgets, and the two leading candidates are trained with three random seeds. title: Open-Vocabulary Models and Label Propagation for Uncertainty-aware Pseudo-Labeling of Object Detection Datasets
authors: Jonathan Klees, Timo Heller, Matthias Rottmann
abstract:
arXiv:2610.29788v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Object detection models rely on large-scale annotated datasets that require substantial manual annotation effort. The labeling costs further increase when annotation uncertainty is captured through soft labels, as multiple annotations must be collected for each object. We address this challenge by introducing a semi-supervised framework for the uncertainty-aware annotation of object detection datasets. Our approach leverages open-vocabulary object detectors to generate region proposals and semantically meaningful object representations. Based on these representations, we construct an object-level similarity graph and propagate probabilistic label information. Our framework assigns soft labels to previously unlabeled objects, quantifying both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Liver Lesion Segmentation and Structured Radiology Reporting
authors: Fatma Ahmed Mansour, Rahatara Ferdousi, Manar Fathy Elshenawy
abstract:
arXiv:2610.34599v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Despite advances in automated liver lesion segmentation, a gap remains between image-derived predictions and clinically interpretable radiology reports. Bridging this gap requires quantitative measurements that are both reproducible and traceable. We present an evidence-grounded agentic AI framework that connects liver and lesion segmentation with deterministic quantification and structured reporting. TotalSegmentator-based nnU-Net models delineate the liver, Couinaud segments, and lesions, while computational tools extract volumes, dimensions, counts, and anatomical locations. A large language model (LLM) organizes these measurements into a predefined reporting schema, with numerical consistency checks against source measurements. On 51 LiTS cases, the segmentation stage achieved a liver Dice score of 0.947, lesion sensitivity of 75.6%, and positive predictive value of 68.9%. title: Sexual dimorphism and sex-specific features of pediatric hand bone shapes via statistical shape modeling
authors: Edwin Tay, Amir A. Zadpoor, Nazli T\"umer

Abstract: Understanding the envelope of shape variation encompassing both sexual dimorphism and growth-related changes in living tissue is a non-trivial task. title: Knowledge-structured and evidence-aware semantic self-distillation for glomerular pathology foundation model

Abstract: Visual foundation models learn rich pathological morphology but lack explicit concept-level supervision. Vision--language pretraining can provide this supervision but requires costly image--text pairs. Here, we introduce GloSAGE, a semantic self-distillation framework that uses lesion profiles predicted by a pretrained visual teacher to construct structured pathology descriptions. Reliability-guided selection identifies image--text anchors, while Knowledge-Structured Pathology Text Synthesis and Evidence-Guided Negative-pair Construction account for partially observed lesions. Image--text alignment trains projection layers while retaining the frozen visual encoder; an intermediate Semantic Transfer Layer supplies features for downstream tasks. title: Seeing and Imagining as One: Unified Video Generation and 4D Perception for Embodied World Modeling
authors: Haitang Feng, Zhuoman Liu, Zhennan Wang, Sheng Wang, Juelin Li, Chengzhi Zhao, Hexiang Wei, Lin Shao

Abstract: Embodied world models should not only imagine plausible futures, but also perceive the geometric, semantic, and motion structure of the evolving world. We present GenSight, a unified embodied world model that brings future video generation and dense perception into a single pretrained video diffusion transformer. GenSight uses a unified spatiotemporal representation for video, depth, embodiment segmentation, and first-frame-relative 2D flow. Built on a shared DiT backbone, GenSight uses lightweight task modulation to predict all modalities within the same architecture. All tasks are jointly optimized within a unified velocity prediction space. title: WildOS: Open-Vocabulary Object Search in the Wild
authors: Hardik Shah, Manthan Patel, Erica Tevere, Deegan Atha, Marcel Kaufmann, Shehryar Khattak, Marco Hutter, Jonas Frey, Patrick Spieler
abstract:
arXiv:2602.19308v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Autonomous navigation in complex, unstructured outdoor environments requires robots to operate over long ranges without prior maps and limited depth sensing. In such settings, relying solely on geometric frontiers for exploration is often insufficient. In such settings, the ability to reason semantically about where to go and what is safe to traverse is crucial for robust, efficient exploration. This work presents WildOS, a unified system for long-range, open-vocabulary object search that combines safe geometric exploration with semantic visual reasoning. WildOS builds a sparse navigation graph to maintain spatial memory, while utilizing a foundation-model-based vision module, ExploRFM, to score frontier nodes of the graph. title: Towards Diverse and Comprehensive Benchmarks for Mutual Information Estimation
authors: Alberto Foresti, Ivan Butakov, Alexander Tolmachev, Giulio Franzese, Alexey Frolov, Pietro Michiardi
abstract:
arXiv:2607.03487v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Mutual information estimation is a central problem in machine learning and statistics; however, existing benchmarks typically evaluate estimators on simplified, low-dimensional distributions, leaving their performance on complex, realistic data largely unexplored. We address this gap with a comprehensive benchmarking framework grounded in a unified copula-theoretic perspective that subsumes existing benchmarks as special cases. Within this framework, we propose two complementary families of tests: a copula-first family that systematically varies ground-truth mutual information, dimensionality, and marginal complexity using synthetic and flow-based transformations; and a marginals-first family that couples real-world image data with controlled dependency structures, extending the classic same-class-pairing paradigm. authors: Dominic Behling, Jonas Hein, Matthias Seibold
abstract:

Abstract: Surgical scene understanding is a prerequisite for context-aware and intelligent systems in the operating room. Current methods rely mostly on visual data, although sound carries complementary information on surgical activity. This work investigates whether the active instrument can be localised from a single microphone and a camera by learning the correspondence between the appearance and sound of surgical instruments. We adapt weakly supervised audio-visual localisation, which learns from the co-occurrence of image and sound, to the surgical setting. Trained without any spatial annotation, the model predicts a heatmap over the sounding instrument. title: Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines
authors: Caleb N. Ellington, Jiaqi Wang, Sohan Addagudi, Elijah Cole
abstract:
arXiv:2610.40700v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: To rigorously establish the value of a novel deep learning method, it must be compared against appropriate baselines. As deep learning has become increasingly common in the physical and life sciences, there have been numerous cases in which apparent progress has turned out to be an artifact of omitted or missing baselines. In this work, we investigate whether this problem can be mitigated by using large language models to automate the construction of baselines. We assemble 36 supervised classification and regression tasks from peer-reviewed studies in Nature, Science, and Cell-family journals that investigate novel deep learning methods for scientific applications. We then use a language model to construct simple baselines for each task. title: A Theoretical Framework for Understanding and Building "Any-task inference" Capable Foundation Models

authors: Christine Ling, Juba Ziani
abstract:

Abstract: Recommendation systems that optimize for the average user can fail to capture the preferences of diverse demographic groups. authors: Huancheng Chen, Xiaodi Sun, Zhaoqiong Huang, Michelle Chang, Jingwen Lu
abstract:

title: CAP: Learning to Optimize from Sparse Observations of Related Tasks
authors: Lin Fu, Siwei Fu, Dong Ni
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41173v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In experiment-driven black-box optimization, each evaluation can consume materials, equipment time, and other resources, limiting the number of experiments available for a new task. Records from completed related optimization campaigns could help, but learning a sequential query policy remains challenging when task-specific experience consists of only a few sparse histories. We propose CAP (Candidate Acquisition Policy), which models shared structure and task-specific variation in fixed historical records to sample interactive practice functions. On these functions, CAP learns a feedback-conditioned query policy aimed at final optimization performance under a fixed evaluation budget. At deployment, its parameters remain fixed while each new observation informs the next query. authors: Angxiu Ni
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41243v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a divergence-kernel method for jointly optimizing neural SDE drift and diffusion fields and the initial Gaussian distribution, using losses that depend directly on the terminal density. In two- and eight-dimensional Gaussian-mixture experiments, we learn time-independent fields and obtain far fewer off-mode samples than score-based generators with similar parameter counts. The drift attracts samples toward the modes, while the diffusion helps disperse excess probability between them.

authors: Hanshuai Cui, Zhiqing Tang, Zhi Yao, Weijia Jia, Jun Luo
abstract:

Abstract: Web platforms such as digital libraries, online stores and university sites must classify new pages before anyone labels them. authors: Micha{\l} Romaszewski, Przemys{\l}aw G{\l}omb
abstract:

Abstract: Tsetlin Machines offer an interpretable, hardware-friendly alternative to conventional machine learning models, but applying them to continuous hyperspectral measurements requires converting spectral signals into Boolean representations. Standard binarisation methods typically discretise each spectral band independently, potentially discarding important relationships between neighbouring wavelengths. authors: Mahmoud S. Mayaleh, Samer A. Mayaleh
abstract:

Abstract: Small-scale sentiment classification often suffers from data scarcity, which limits the generalization ability of the models. This study evaluates and compares the effectiveness of three data augmentation strategies: Easy Data Augmentation (EDA), back-translation, and contextual token substitution (nlpaug-style), with both traditional machine learning classifiers (Logistic Regression, Random Forest) and transformer-based models (BERT). authors: Mila Gorecki, Moritz Hardt
abstract:

Abstract: Language models face two opposing concerns: monoculture, in which models err in correlated ways, and multiplicity, in which equally accurate models make conflicting decisions. authors: Yukiya Horiba, Hakaze Cho, Takahiro Yakoh
abstract:

Abstract: Task Vectors (TVs) provide a compact way to steer large language models, but they are typically treated as atomized directions merely extracted from hidden states, leaving their internal functional structure poorly understood. title: Implicit Assumptions About Tasks in Continual Learning
authors: Kathrin Korte, Christian Metzner, Akshay Bedhotiya, Viet Anh Khoa Tran, Eleni Nisioti, Sebastian Risi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.41792v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Continual learning is the study of how a model accumulates knowledge from data received over time, rather than all at once. In practice, this is typically achieved by dividing a dataset into tasks and presenting them sequentially. Explanations of the resulting measurements take into account factors such as the similarity between segments, the rate at which the data changes and the order of presentation. title: Backpropagation-free Deep Learning for Time-Series Classification

abstract:

abstract:

Abstract: Tabular transformer models such as TabPFN achieve strong predictive performance but incur substantial inference costs, making them difficult to deploy in resource-constrained settings. title: Neural Networks Based on Power Method and Inverse Power Method for Solving Linear Eigenvalue Problems
authors: Qihong Yang, Yangtao Deng, Yu Yang, Qiaolin He, Shiquan Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2209.11134v5 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: In this article, we propose two kinds of neural networks inspired by power method and inverse power method to solve linear eigenvalue problems. These neural networks share similar ideas with traditional methods, in which the differential operator is realized by automatic differentiation. The eigenfunction of the eigenvalue problem is learned by the neural network and the iterative algorithms are implemented by optimizing the specially defined loss function. The largest positive eigenvalue, smallest eigenvalue and interior eigenvalues with the given prior knowledge can be solved efficiently. We examine the applicability and accuracy of our methods in the numerical experiments in one dimension, two dimensions and higher dimensions. title: The Geometry of Multitask Learning: Sharp Rates for Shared Subspace Estimation
authors: Tony Cai, Abhinav Chakraborty, Samory Kpotufe
abstract:
arXiv:2610.40713v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Learning a shared subspace in multitask learning is an important statistical problem, yet exact rates remain poorly understood in many of the formal settings considered in the literature. To address this gap, which arises from limitations of existing upper-bound techniques, we propose a general multitask lemma. The lemma provides sufficient conditions for fast subspace estimation in generic multitask settings, in the form of geometric conditions on the task regression functions and their estimators. We subsequently show that the multitask lemma yields sharp minimax rates---previously unknown---for linear regression and classification in the regimes considered, and rates matching up to logarithmic factors for additive-noise regression.

title: DNNs, Dataset Statistics, and Correlation Functions
authors: Robert W. Batterman, James F. Woodward
abstract:
arXiv:2511.21715v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: This paper argues that dataset structure is important in image recognition tasks (among other tasks). Specifically, we focus on the nature and genesis of correlational structure in the actual datasets upon which DNNs are trained. We argue that DNNs are implementing a widespread methodology in condensed matter physics and materials science that focuses on mesoscale correlation structures that live between fundamental atomic/molecular scales and continuum scales. Specifically, we argue that DNNs that are successful in image classification must be discovering high order correlation functions. It is well-known that DNNs successfully generalize in apparent contravention of standard statistical learning theory. We consider the implications of our discussion for this puzzle.

abstract:

Abstract: We study neural networks (NNs) operating under hardware-induced memory faults and computational errors, which can degrade reliability in safety-critical applications. Our approach imposes structured real-valued linear constraints on network weights, enabling efficient error detection and recovery without increasing the number of parameters or compromising classification performance. The proposed method leverages linear programming and sparse recovery techniques to achieve low-complexity error correction. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first real-number-based ECC scheme that simultaneously addresses memory and computational errors in neural networks.
